entries.sourceText: The truth is that everyone is bored, and devotes himself to cultivating habits.
entries.translationZh: 事实是，人人都感到无聊，并把自己投入到习惯的培养之中。

entries.sourceText: You can get through the days there without trouble, once you have formed habits.
entries.translationZh: 一旦形成习惯，你就能在那里顺利地度过每一天。

entries.sourceText: Without memories, without hope, they lived for the moment only.
entries.translationZh: 没有记忆，也没有希望，他们只为眼前这一刻而活。

entries.sourceText: Indeed, the here and now had come to mean everything to them.
entries.translationZh: 的确，此时此地已经成了他们的一切。

entries.sourceText: The thing was to do your job as it should be done.
entries.translationZh: 重要的是把自己的工作做到它应有的样子。

entries.sourceText: You get married, you go on loving a bit longer, you work.
entries.translationZh: 人们结婚，再爱上一阵子，然后工作。

entries.sourceText: And you work so hard that it makes you forget to love.
entries.translationZh: 你如此拼命工作，以至于忘记了去爱。

entries.sourceText: But it's no reason for giving up the struggle.
entries.translationZh: 但这并不是放弃斗争的理由。

entries.sourceText: But perhaps we should love what we cannot understand.
entries.translationZh: 也许，我们应该去爱那些自己无法理解的事物。

entries.sourceText: And in his corner Rambert savored that bitter sense of freedom which comes of total deprivation.
entries.translationZh: 在自己的角落里，朗贝尔品尝着彻底失去之后那种苦涩的自由感。

entries.sourceText: Well, personally, I've seen enough of people who die for an idea.
entries.translationZh: 就我个人而言，我已经看够了那些为一种观念而死的人。

entries.sourceText: There's no question of heroism in all this. It's a matter of common decency.
entries.translationZh: 这一切无关英雄主义，只关乎普通人的正派。

entries.sourceText: The only means of righting a plague is—common decency.
entries.translationZh: 纠正一场瘟疫的唯一办法，是普通人的正派。

entries.sourceText: But it may be shameful to be happy by oneself.
entries.translationZh: 但一个人独自幸福，也许是可耻的。

entries.sourceText: Perhaps because I, too, would like to do my bit for happiness.
entries.translationZh: 也许是因为，我也愿意为幸福尽自己的一份力。

entries.sourceText: That, too, is why this epidemic has taught me nothing new, except that I must fight it at your side.
entries.translationZh: 所以，这场疫病没有教给我什么新东西，只让我明白必须与你并肩对抗它。

entries.sourceText: And since they could not be thinking of their death all the time, they thought of nothing.
entries.translationZh: 因为他们不可能一直想着自己的死亡，于是便什么也不想。

entries.sourceText: There are more things to admire in men than to despise.
entries.translationZh: 在人身上，值得赞美的东西多于值得蔑视的东西。
